summary.headline: Week 1 went exactly to plan (41.99 of 42 km), but the week 2 tempo ended at 6 km with sharp calf pain and RPE 9.
observations: Week 1 was clean: 4 of 4 sessions as planned and 41.99 km against 42.0 km. Easy runs were even at 5:42-5:50/km, and the 16 km long run was a steady 5:48/km at HR 142.
The Nov 3 tempo was on target: 4 km at 4:37/km, HR 161-162, with a controlled warm-up and cool-down.
On Nov 10 the tempo was stopped at 6.0 km of 9 planned, with sharp calf pain and RPE 9. The 'sessions completed' count is 1 of 4 for week 2.

The tempo block was run at 5:00/km, about 23 s/km slower than the 4:37 target, yet HR averaged 176 (max 179). On Nov 3 the same session at 4:37/km sat at HR 161-162. Much higher HR at a slower pace points to the calf problem or fatigue rather than a pacing mistake.
The final km dropped to 7:00/km, consistent with stopping because of pain.
The 47.99 km logged against 425.5 km planned is mostly future weeks, not misses. The real concern is the injury, 9 weeks out from a race on 2027-01-10.
Your notes flag mild left achilles tightness last spring. This is a calf complaint, a different but neighbouring area, so it deserves caution.
suggestions: Don't run through this. Skip or replace Thursday's 10 km easy run and only resume once walking and daily activity are pain-free. Consider having a physio or doctor look at the calf.
When you restart, drop the quality sessions first. Run short, flat, easy runs (about 5:50-6:13/km) before bringing back tempo or intervals.
Treat the 17 km long run planned for Nov 15 as optional. Build back up to your Week 1 volume (about 42 km) rather than jumping to 45 km or more.
If a few weeks are lost, ask for the plan to be re-cut. A shorter build, or a later race, would be safer than compressing the peak weeks, especially as 1:30 was already a stretch goal.
Log RPE and a short note after every run, including any calf or achilles feel, so changes in load are easier to spot early.
